utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-95-13/1-A, the Prosecutor versus Mile Mrksic and Veselin Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now have the appearances of the parties. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Good morning -- good afternoon, Your Honour. Matteo Costi, appearing for the Prosecution, with senior appeals counsel Helen Brady and our case manager Sebastiaan van Hooydonk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Costi. Now, counsel for Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon to my learned friends from the Prosecution and everybody in the courtroom. Miroslav Vasic appearing for Mr. Mrksic. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vasic. Now I gathered that we do not have in court counsel for Mr. Sljivancanin or we do?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: We do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, I'm very happy to see you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: We do, Mr. President. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I must say this has come to me somewhat as a surprise because I understand it was not --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I've been assigned on this case to help Mr. Novak Lukic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: No, no, I was not aware that you would be in court today since Mr. Sljivancanin --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I thought Mr. Lukic would have advised the Court. I'm sorry, Mr. President but representing Mr. Sljivancanin this afternoon is myself, Stephane Bourgon, accompanied by William St-Michel, who is from Quebec, Canada, an intern working with us on this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Quebec, Canada, is very far from the country you are used to. In any event, I am pleased to see you and as our Scheduling Order indicated, the counsel for Mr. Sljivancanin was invited to be here but we did not compel presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: This is, as we all know, a Status Conference called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Rule 65 bis (B) requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days of the filing of a notice of appeal in order to allow any person in custody pending appeal to raise issues of concern. The conference is also an opportunity for the Tribunal to inquire about the mental and physical condition of the detained person. Mr. Mrksic, filed his notice of appeal on 29th October, 2007, and he remains in custody. Mr. Sljivancanin filed his notice of appeal on the same day, but pursuant to a decision of 11 December 2007 he's currently on provisional release. I would like to begin the Status Conference by inquiring into Mr. Mrksic's health. Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you very much for raising this issue. I have spoken with Mr. Mrksic, he is in good health, but I believe that he himself would like to address you and personally confirm this to you and maybe tell you something about his conditions of detention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vasic. Yes, I will be -- I am ready to hear Mr. Mrksic. Mr. Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT MRKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, since I am addressing you for the first time, I have already raised the problems that I have had in the past. For the time being, I'm feeling well --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It is very difficult to hear the accused, it seems that his microphone is not on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Or the accused is too far from the microphone, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I'm hearing him loud and clear. It's everything all right. You can continue now.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT MRKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is the first time I am appearing before you as the Presiding Judge and I would like to repeat what I've already spoken before previously in the courtroom. I arrived here in 2002 in the month of May after an open-heart surgery when I had two by-pass stints introduced. In the course of my case I had a heart attack, I was taken to the hospital in Leiden, and I had two more stints. I am currently feeling well, but the nature of my illness is such that you never know when the problems may appear again. As far as the Detention Unit is concerned, I don't have any remarks or objections to my stay there, and I don't know what else to tell you. I have not been provisionally released save for the 48 hours that I spent at home when my mother died. I have -- I'm experiencing certain problems at the moment. I don't know whether I'm going to be filing a motion for provisional release. I'm working on my defence together with my lawyer, Mr. Vasic. I believe that we have achieved certain progress and I would like to thank you for hearing me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mrksic, you can sit down, and I was glad that you are feeling better and I hope that your good health will continue and I wish you a very good health. We on our part in a fairly complicated case are trying to move things forward as rapidly as possible, I will say something about that in a moment. But first I would like to turn to the counsel for Mr. Sljivancanin and ask whether they have any concerns that they would like to raise. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. On behalf of Mr. Sljivancanin I can report that he is doing fine being as presently being on provisional release. He is complying fully with all conditions set in the provisional release order of December 2007. He is sending his regards both to yourself, Mr. President, and to the Appeals Chamber and he has asked me to be present this afternoon out of courtesy for the Appeals Chamber. We have nothing else to report. Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. As I told you earlier I was very pleased to see you indeed and I thank you for the good wishes that you have conveyed to me. I want to ask the Prosecutor at this stage whether they have any other issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Costi.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Prosecution does not have any other issue to submit to your attention. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Costi. Let me say then since there are no other issues, a few words to the parties about scheduling. I am sure you are all aware how the schedule works, but let me go through it again now. First on the Prosecution's appeal, the Prosecution has already submitted its appeals brief pursuant to the decision of 14 December 2007. The responses are due 20 days after Mr. Mrksic and Mr. Sljivancanin have received the B/C/S translation of the trial judgement. I gather that the translation will be available at some point next month, namely, during the month of March. Second, the appeal briefs of Mr. Mrksic and Mr. Sljivancanin are due 40 days after they have received the translation of the trial judgement. I believe from the conversations so far that the parties have no other issues that they would like to raise now. And I take it that applies also to Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Maybe just two very brief things. From our learned friends from the Prosecution we have received two disclosures with some statements. This is what was done earlier today. I would like to know whether these disclosures have been part of the documents that the Prosecutor announced in their declaration that they filed according to Rule 111(B), in which they stated that some documents were being disclosed according to the Rule A -- 89(i) [as interpreted]. That is the first issue that I would like to raise, and the second issue --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Let me ask the Prosecution to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Your Honour, we made a declaration when we filed our appeal brief, and these disclosure that we just tendered to the Defence in these two days is the result of our ongoing obligation to review material, and so we were aware of it only two or three days ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Costi. This resolves the first question, doesn't it? Okay, the second matter, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. My second issue is this: I am fully aware of your decision regarding the dead-lines for the appeal brief and response to the appeal brief by the Prosecutor. I am trying -- I'll try and slow down for the interpretation. The Defence would certainly find things much easier if these dead-lines did not overlap because in addition to working on the appeal brief we also have to translate the appeal brief filed by the Prosecutor because these are not officially translated and we have to do it for the benefit of our client. And that is why I am trying to share with you my conclusion, which is that it would be much easier for the Defence if these dead-lines did not overlap because if that was not the case we will have to work on three things, we will have to work on translating the Prosecutor's brief to our clients, to work on the reply to the Prosecutor's appeal brief, and to prepare our own appeal brief, and all these dead-lines fall after the first-instance Chamber decision has been made available to our client in B/C/S. It would be our kind request to extend the dead-line for the reply to the Prosecutor's appeal brief to a time after the Prosecutor's appeal brief has been filed. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, I'm really anxious to have this case move forward expeditiously towards a hearing, especially after hearing what your client said about his state of health. However, if you feel very strongly about this matter, submit a motion and we will look at that. And please submit that motion if you only feel that you really have to, because I'm quite sure that your client would like to have his day in court as soon as possible. Mr. Costi.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The issue has been discussed already in the filing that we are aware of, so we -- just for the record we stay with our -- we oppose to this request because there is no reason for which they cannot start working right now and the overlapping in itself is not a violation of their right. And in any case they still have the right to submit a further motion in a written form in the future if they found it necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Costi. There is a lot of time that I think that the counsel for the appellant can use working on the briefs. He can do that already, and I draw his attention to the language used in my order of 14 December 2007. Again, should Mr. Vasic feel very strongly about it and feel that our position on that should be revisited, by all means you are entitled to submit a brief. Please, again do it only in case of real necessity because I believe that my job as a Pre-Appeal Judge here is really in this case particularly to move it forward rapidly. Mr. Vasic, I see you trying to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We will first do our utmost to do our job as efficiently as possible, and only if absolutely necessary we will file our motion as you have allowed us to do. In any case, we are going to try and comply with your absolutely perfect decision, with your order, as you have mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. I gathered that the counsel for Mr. Sljivancanin has no comments on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President. We have no comments. Work is in progress on both the response to the Prosecution appeal and our own appellant's brief. That being said, Mr. Sljivancanin insists on being fully informed and involved in the preparation and the briefing of his appeal, and as the situation progresses we will see if there is a need for further motion. However, at this time we take good note of your guidance and we will do our utmost to comply. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Bourgon. If there are no further issues to raise on behalf of either of the appellants, I believe that we can conclude our business today, and I thank the parties for their attendance and call the proceedings to a close. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: adjourned at 4.19 p.m.
